text:
Joel Armia has become the player The Hockey Writers say the Kings' penalty kill needs more of, on a unit they called historically bad. He's 33, in his second season in Los Angeles, and playing about 13 and a half minutes a night.

He has six points in 15 games, with goals against Ottawa and San Jose in the last two weeks. His finishing is close to his chances (three goals on 2.2 expected, the quality of his chances), and the Kings have scored 4.5 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, which has cost him points. Los Angeles has about half the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, roughly even with the team.

Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with weak offensive impact (bottom 6% of forwards). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush. His value is the work without the puck, on a team that needs it. Our projection sees about 15 goals.
